page: Amazon Web Services x8g.large is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1809.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3226.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3403.38. Memory performance is mixed; while the large-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 53.78 GB/sec, the write bandwidth is weak at 21.69 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.38 GB/sec, but multi-threaded decompression drops to a weak relative standing of 27.28 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are poor, with prompt processing at 145.88 tokens/sec and text generation at 38.74 tokens/sec for a small 135M model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x8g.large offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel CPU processing. The lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps are key architectural tradeoffs. This profile is appropriate for caching layers, lightweight database operations, and memory-intensive single-threaded applications, as reflected in its average Passmark database operations score of 2990.22.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.large is an ARM64 memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on an AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. This configuration delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmarks show average single-core CPU and read memory bandwidth performance, contrasted by weak multi-core scaling and weak memory write speeds. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong, while database operations and text processing perform at average levels. Given the high memory density and limited CPU parallelization, the x8g.large is best suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads such as caching, small database nodes, and single-threaded data processing.
